chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man and 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sa'id ibn Yasar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We mix with people from Ahl al-Sawad and others, and we sell to them, earning ten for twelve and ten for thirteen, and we make that binding between us and them for a year or thereabouts. So the man writes for us on his house or on his land with that money which contains the surplus that he took from us as a pledge (shira'), having sold and taken the price. We promise him: if he brings the money to a set time between us and him, we will return the pledge to him; and if the time comes and he does not bring us the dirhams, then it is ours. What do you think about the pledge? He said: 'I think it is yours if he does not act (pay), and if he brings the money for the time, then return it to him.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ اَلسَّوَاد: The people of the marshes (a historical region in Iraq), used here to denote specific local traders
key_terms.اَلشِّرَاء: Pledge or security given to guarantee a debt or obligation
key_terms.اَلْعَشَرَةَ بِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ: Ten for twelve, a common idiom for a 20% markup or profit margin on credit sales
key_terms.قَدْ بَاعَ وَ قَبَضَ: Having sold and taken possession (of the price/goods), indicating the completion of the initial transaction

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on keeping pledged property if a buyer defaults on a credit sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *bay' al-mu'ajjal* (credit sale) with a markup, a common practice among merchants interacting with the 'Ahl al-Sawad' (often referring to rural or non-urban populations). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the use of a pledged asset (*shira'*) as security for the debt, establishing a clear conditional mechanism: the pledge becomes the seller's property upon default, but must be returned if the buyer fulfills the obligation on time. This ruling provides practical legal certainty for early Shia merchants engaging in deferred payment contracts with collateral.
